newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Key Albania party wants full vote monitoring.
newsitem.headline: Key Albania party wants full vote monitoring.

text.p: Albania's Socialist Party, the second largest in a nine-party national unity government, said on Wednesday it would take part in elections at the end of June if there was full international monitoring.

Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano said that if full and proper monitoring guaranteed valid elections then his party would take part even under a disputed election law that has caused most parties to threaten to boycott the vote.
The elections are regarded as vital to stop Albania sliding back into the riots and looting that swept the country last March after anger over collapsed pyramid schemes turned into rebellion.

"If we have this kind of positive answer by (European envoy Franz) Vranitzky and the international community that a joint action model can be applied for Albanian elections then we need nothing more," Nano told Reuters.
The comments seemed to be the first sign of movement in a long-running crisis over the elections.
The Socialists and most governement parties threatened to boycott the vote over election rules they say favour President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party.
Prime Minister Bashkim Fino has been heading marathon talks to end the crisis.
